item.title: At least 12 states report cyberattacks on water systems possibly linked to Iran
item.description: Cyberattacks on U.S. water systems that officials suspect may be linked to Iran-backed hackers have been reported in at least a dozen states, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: Jewish Insider editor-in-chief says DSA's weaknesses go "beyond antisemitism"
item.description: The relationship between progressive candidates and Jewish voters has been a central focus this election cycle. Jewish Insider Editor in-Chief Josh Kraushaar joins "The Takeout" to discuss his new piece titled: "DSA's Achilles' Heel Goes Beyond Antisemitism."

item.title: New Mexico attorney general explains why he's suing DOJ over Epstein files
item.description: New Mexico is suing the Trump administration for access to files related to Jeffrey Epstein as it investigates the convicted sex offender's Zorro Ranch property. New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Clancy family nanny testifies that Lindsay was "a wonderful mom"
item.description: The last nanny who worked for the Clancy family testified at trial that Lindsay was a wonderful mom who loved her children.

item.title: Trump says Strait of Hormuz deal could happen as soon as today amid talks
item.description: President Trump told reporters Tuesday evening that an announcement on the Strait of Hormuz could happen today or tomorrow, following talks between Iran and Oman.

item.title: Trump again teases deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz, but likelihood remains unclear
item.description: President Trump is touting progress on the potential reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and says a deal could be made as soon as Wednesday. CBS News national security analyst Aaron MacLean joins "The Takeout" with more.

item.title: Michigan sees record midterm primary turnout
item.description: Michiganders on Tuesday set a midterm primary turnout record, with a whopping 2.5 million voters casting ballots. CBS News election law contributor David Becker joins "The Takeout" with more.

item.title: Progressive who won Michigan House primary says voters are "sick of corporate-funded candidates"
item.description: The progressive primary winner in Michigan's 7th Congressional District, William Lawrence, won 44% of the vote, while his two establishment challengers together attracted 56%. Lawrence joins "The Takeout" to reflect on his victory and to look ahead to November's general election.

item.title: El-Sayed looks to unite Democrats after Senate primary victory
item.description: Progressive Abdul El-Sayed is looking ahead to November's general election after narrowly defeating moderate Haley Stevens in Tuesday's Michigan Democratic Senate primary. CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe has the latest from Detroit.

item.title: Anthropic's Mythos AI created fake profiles to trick people in hack, then hid evidence
item.description: Two of the most powerful artificial intelligence agents created fake human profiles to try to trick people in attempted cyberattacks. Mashable tech editor Tim Werth joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: As FDA approves marketing for nicotine pouches, some doctors sound alarms
item.description: One health advocate called nicotine pouches a "profound risk" for young people.

item.title: Water system cyberattacks spread to at least 12 states
item.description: Several states are experiencing cyberattacks on their water systems after Minnesota reported at attack last week. CBS News homeland security correspondent Nicole Sganga has the latest.

item.title: Video shows rare tiger shark catch and release in New Jersey
item.description: A new video shows two men handling a tiger shark on a beach in New Jersey. CBS News' Lilia Luciano has more on the encounter.

item.title: FAA probing Marine One safety incident around National Airport
item.description: When the helicopter that transports President Trump crosses the Potomac, Reagan Washington National Airport is required to impose a ground stop on air traffic.

item.title: Inside the eBay stalking scandal | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: Last week eBay agreed to pay $55.7 million to a Massachusetts couple that was the victim of a bizarre harassment and cyberstalking campaign orchestrated by former employees of the company. In 2023, 60 Minutes spoke with the couple, Ina and David Steiner.

item.title: Some Gen Zers swap smartphones for "dumb" phones in a bid to unplug
item.description: "It really opens up your mind," said one 23-year-old who ditched smartphones to wean herself off social media.

item.title: Senate confirms Dr. Erica Schwartz as CDC director
item.description: The Senate confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz in a 51 to 44 vote.

item.title: Why increased AI spending caused SpaceX shares to fall
item.description: CBS News business contributor Javier David breaks down why SpaceX shares fell on Wednesday after the company announced higher spending on AI in its earnings report.

item.title: Popular influencer shot dead during livestream outside restaurant
item.description: Cesar Gastelum, who had more than 600,000 followers on TikTok, was broadcasting with two friends when he was killed.

item.title: Washington braces for weather that could fuel catastrophic fires
item.description: As wind conditions worsen, Washington officials are concerned that firefighters may have an even harder time containing the devastating fires burning the Spokane area. CBS News' Kris Van Cleave and Jessica Burch report.

item.title: Trump claims Strait of Hormuz deal could happen soon as Iran and Oman engage in talks
item.description: President Trump told reporters "a lot of progress had been made" on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and suggested a deal could be announced as early as Wednesday. CBS News' Natalie Brand has the details.

item.title: Perez Hilton hospitalized after livestreaming acts of self-harm, officials say
item.description: In the livestream, which has since been taken down, Hilton appears to be bloodied and in a distressed mental state.

item.title: $25 million reward offered for U.S.-born leader of powerful cartel
item.description: Juan Carlos González is the stepson of "El Mencho," who was killed by the Mexican military.

item.title: Progressive Abdul El-Sayed projected to win Michigan Democratic Senate primary
item.description: Former state health official Abdul El-Sayed faced Rep. Haley Stevens in the Democratic Senate primary in Michigan in a closely watched contest that represented the latest test of the party's divisions.

item.title: Baby "cocaine hippo" linked to infamous drug lord is rescued in Colombia
item.description: Colombia has around 200 so-called "cocaine hippos" living in the wild, all of which descended from a colony brought to South America by slain cocaine kingpin Pablo Escobar.

item.title: Record-low Danube River levels threaten shutdown of Hungary's nuclear plant
item.description: Three of four units of Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant were not in operation and the fourth was operating at about 50%, as of Wednesday morning.

item.title: Disney partners with TikTok to offer creator content on its app
item.description: Disney and TikTok are teaming up to let users create short-form videos that draw on the entertainment giant's large stable of movies and TV shows.

item.title: House Democrats targeting 12 new GOP districts, including Lauren Boebert's seat
item.description: With 90 days until the midterm elections, House Democrats are expanding the map of Republican-held congressional districts they believe they can potentially flip this fall.

item.title: White House declassifies info on secret FBI probe into Trump's firing of Comey
item.description: The White House has declassified information claiming the FBI probed whether President Trump acted as a Russian asset when he fired James Comey, a theory an administration official said wasn't backed up by evidence.

item.title: Inside a California data center as communities raise concerns about energy costs
item.description: California lawmakers are considering several proposals affecting data centers, including bills intended to shield utility customers from increased electricity costs.
